title: PII exposure scanner and delayed scrub orchestrator for ad-hoc console analytics
creator: Samira Bhandari
description:
Problem: Ad-hoc console dashboards and one-off analytics queries sometimes introduce PII into long-lived analytic tables and BI exports. Current retention/deletion pipelines focus on lineage-based erasure and scheduled backfills, which miss transient exposures created by queries or temporary aggregations. We need an automated guard that detects PII exposure patterns in analytics outputs and provides a controlled 'delayed scrub' flow to remove or obfuscate the exposed artifacts after a short review window.

Scope: Build a PII exposure scanner that runs as part of the analytics export and nightly job graph, and a delayed-scrub orchestrator that: (1) creates an evidence package and marks artifacts for review, (2) waits for a configurable review window (default 72h), (3) performs reversible pseudonymization or deletion depending on review outcome, (4) emits attestation logs for compliance and audit exports. This ticket covers backend services, orchestration, and the minimal console hooks to surface exposures to reviewers. UI/UX and extensive RBAC will be follow-ups (separate tickets).

Goals:
- Detect high-confidence PII patterns (emails, phone numbers, keys, SSNs, names with high entropy) in ad-hoc exports and derived tables.
- Surface findings with context (query id, exporter, sample rows) to reviewers in Console.
- Orchestrate a delayed scrub flow with safe rollback window via reversible pseudomap for 7 days.
- Produce tamper-evident audit artifacts for legal/compliance teams.

Non-Goals: Real-time blocking of queries, broad UI redesign, wide RBAC rules. Those will be handled by separate PM tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Scanner is integrated into nightly analytics exporter and flags PII exposures with severity tags (high/medium/low)
Each flagged artifact has an evidence package (query_id, schema, sample rows, detector confidence) stored in the evidence store
Delayed-scrub orchestrator exposes a review window defaulting to 72 hours and transitions artifacts to pseudonymization or deletion after confirmation or timeout
Reversible pseudomap persists mapping for 7 days and is cryptographically sealed; deletion path fully removes rows and records an attestation
Audit export contains immutable attestations for every scrub action (who/what/when/reason) and is queryable by compliance team
Integration tests cover scanner false positive rate threshold (<5% on baseline test corpus) and scrub orchestration end-to-end
tasks: Design PII detection heuristics and select open-source detectors (regexes, ML model) - coordinate with Applied ML
Implement scanner microservice (k8s job) that consumes analytics export topic and emits findings to evidence-store
Build evidence-store schema (S3 + metadata index) and attach sample artifacts and query provenance
Implement delayed-scrub orchestrator (state machine) with review window, action rules, and attestation emitter
Add reversible pseudomap service with HMAC-sealed mappings and TTL enforcement
Wire audit attestation exporter to compliance S3 bucket and build basic query API for compliance team
End-to-end integration tests + canary run on dev org before rollout

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives will create reviewer fatigue - Mitigation: tiered severity and ML-based confidence scoring; provide bulk dismiss with rationale
Risk: Reversible mapping misuse could leak PII - Mitigation: require key access control, KMS usage for private deployments, TTL enforcement and audit logs
Risk: Large exports could overwhelm scanner - Mitigation: sampling + backpressure on analytics exporter topic and horizontal scaling policy
